intended_object: A bundled "presentation" record. It pairs the subgroup `points A` of GL₂₇(A) (the A-points of the type-E₆ minuscule carrier) with the proof `points_def A` that this subgroup equals the subgroup cut out by the integral Hopf ideal `definingIdeal`. Inferred from the docstring, the module documentation and the way the `IntegralPointsPresentation` API is used.
explanation:
`IntegralPointsPresentation n I A` is the subtype `{subgroup : Subgroup (GL (Fin n) A) // subgroup = hopfIdealPointsSubgroup n I A}`. It is a singleton type. Its only job is to let the library reuse a shared API (`map`, `map_comp`, `mulEquiv`, `functor`), so that a concretely defined subgroup can be transported along its proof that it equals the Hopf-ideal points.

`pointsPresentation A` just bundles the already-defined subgroup `points A` with the lemma `points_def A`. The record adds no mathematical content. The real objects are `points` (the A-points of the E₆ minuscule group scheme inside GL₂₇) and `definingIdeal`, and both are defined elsewhere. This declaration is a technical device for internal use: it carries a proof of an equality so that functoriality and representability statements can be applied.

It is therefore not itself a mathematical object to be judged for faithfulness.
